text:
Mexico Open: Karl Vilips shoots 62 to take the first-round lead with Marco Penge two shots back
England's Marco Penge was two shots off leader Karl Vilips after round one of the Mexico Open, while US Open champion Wyndham Clark shot a 69 as the only top 10 player in the field; watch live coverage of round two from 8pm on Sky Sports Golf on Friday
Friday 30 October 2026 07:28, UK
Karl Vilips used two long birdie streaks to take the first-round lead Thursday in the Mexico Open, the first of two straight PGA Tour events in the country.
Vilips shot a nine-under 62 in the afternoon round on the Vidanta Vallarta layout, making five straight birdies on Nos. 11-15 on his opening nine and finishing with four in a row. In between, he had another birdie and a bogey.
The 25-year-old Australian pointed to his driver.
"Had it on a string for the first nine," Vilips said. "Got a little loose in the middle and got it back on course toward the end of the round. It was lift, clean and place today so being in the fairway was a must for me and I took advantage of those drives that I hit."
Kensai Hirata of Japan was a stroke back, and Ben Griffin was at 64 with Marco Penge, Garrick Higgo and Jeffrey Kang.
Alvaro Ortiz of Mexico opened with a 65. He earned his PGA Tour card for next year through the Korn Ferry Tour.
"It was lovely," Ortiz said. "Bogey-free, played really solid. I felt like I was just flowing the whole day. Gave myself a lot of chances. I think I did very well from tee to green, which makes it very nice on this golf course."
Ortiz won the event in 2021 when it was part of the PGA Tour Latinoamerica schedule. The World Wide Technology Championship is next week at El Cardonal at Diamante in Los Cabos.
Vilips won the 2025 Puerto Rico Open for his lone PGA Tour title, making him exempt on the tour through next season.
The former Stanford player is 141st in the FedEx Cup Fall standings, with many players fighting to get into the final top 100 to remain on the tour.
Hirata is trying to move up from 170th. He made a 20-foot eagle putt on No. 3 and holed two birdie putts outside 20 feet.
"It was a perfect 7-wood distance and I hit a perfect 7-wood shot, which left me a really easy left-to-righter," Hirata said about the eagle. "Then that went in and kept the momentum going the rest of the back nine."
Penge is 112th in the standings. He had an 18-foot eagle putt on No. 3.
"I feel like I haven't actually played that much this year," Penge said "I've only played 18 tournaments due to, obviously, health issues. I'm just trying to get back fit really."
Defending champion Brian Campbell shot a 67.
Tom Kim also was at 67. He's playing for the first time since he won the gold medal in the Asian Games, which excuses him from mandatory military serve in South Korea.
U.S. Open champion Wyndham Clark had a 69. He's the only player from the top 10 in the world in the field.
John Daly II, the son of the two-time major champion, opened with a 70. He's playing on a sponsor exemption.

digest_he:
גולפאי האוסטרלי קארל ויפילס פתח בצורה מרשימה את אליפות מקסיקו פתוחה, שהנה התחרות הראשונה מבין שתי תחרויות סבב ה-PGA הרצופות במדינה. ויפילס רשם סבב מצוין עם תוצאה של 62 חבטות, שכלל רצפי חבטות מוצלחים במיוחד בחלקו הראשון והאחרון של המסלול.

במקום השני במרחק שתי חבטות מהמוביל ממוקם האנגלי מרקו פנז, בעוד ששחקנים בולטים נוספים כמו האלוף המכהן בריאן קמפבל ואלוף ארצות הברית ווינדהאם קלארק רשמו תוצאות יציבות. התחרות ממשיכה למשוך אליה שחקני צמרת רבים הנלחמים על מקומם בדירוג הכללי.
